title: Open-Source Large Language Model integration into Clinical Genetics Workflows: Pilot Study
summary:
Background: More and more patients, both children and adults, are being offered genetic testing as healthcare moves towards more personalised treatment. Genetic testing can help doctors understand whether a person's health condition is linked to their genes and identify treatments or care that may be more suitable for them. However, patients often need support from trained genetic counsellors to understand why testing is being offered, what the results might mean, and how these results could affect them and their families. As demand for genetic testing continues to increase, new ways of providing genetic counselling are needed to ensure patients receive the support they need without long waiting times.

Large language models (LLMs), could help address this problem. They may be able to take over or simplify some of the time-consuming tasks involved in genetic counselling, such as preparing documents, gathering information, and researching genetic conditions. This could reduce the workload of genetic counsellors, allowing them to spend more time directly supporting patients and potentially see more patients in less time. However, it is not yet clear whether healthcare professionals and patients would feel comfortable with AI being used as part of genetic counselling. It is also unclear how much time and effort AI could actually save compared with current ways of working.

Primary aim: To investigate whether healthcare professionals find the use of large language models (AI) acceptable in clinical genetics and whether using AI can make genetic counselling processes more efficient and save time.

Secondary aim: To explore whether patients are comfortable with and accept the use of AI as part of their genetic counselling experience.

We expect that both healthcare professionals and patients will find the use of AI in clinical genetics acceptable. We also expect that including AI in current clinical workflows will make certain tasks quicker and more efficient compared with current practice.
conditions: Limited availability and capacity of genetic counselling services

interventions.name: Physicians and allied health professionals will pilot an LLM for use in clinical genetic workflows. One LLM use case has been defined a priori – LLM generation of clinical letters – with further use cases evaluating additional LLM applications within clinical workflows planned. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Physicians delivering genetic counselling and associated allied health professionals; patients attending genetic counselling consultations; for pediatric patients/patients unable to provide consent, parents/legal guardians also attending genetic counselling.
Exclusion criteria:
No specific exclusion criteria.
